364179.title: The spouse-loving Oberwolfach conjecture for four groups of odd cycle length
364179.statement: Let $m$ be a positive odd integer. The spouse-loving variant of the Oberwolfach problem, denoted $\operatorname{OP}^+(n;m)$, asks whether the graph $K_n+I$ admits a $C_m$-factorization, where $I$ is a 1-factor and $C_m$ is a cycle of length $m$. **Spouse-loving Oberwolfach conjecture.** The problem $\operatorname{OP}^+(4m;m)$ has a solution if and only if $m\geq 5$. This is the only case left unresolved by the paper's almost complete solution of the spouse-loving variant of the Oberwolfach problem with uniform cycle lengths.

364256.title: Exceptional-parameter conjecture for biased edge coloring games
364256.statement:
Let $m_1$ and $m_2$ be positive integers satisfying $m_1>m_2$, and suppose that there is no positive integer $k$ such that $m_1=km_2+k-1$. Let $\chi'_g(G;m,1)$ denote the game chromatic index in the $(m,1)$-edge coloring game. **Exceptional-parameter conjecture.** There is a graph $G$ such that

$$
\chi'_g(G;m_1,1)>\chi'_g(G;m_2,1).
$$

This conjecture complements the proposition proving the reverse inequality when $m_1=km_2+k-1$ for some positive integer $k$. It predicts that every remaining parameter pair admits a graph witnessing a strict increase, and the source provides no resolution.

364405.title: The induced-cycle conjecture for triangle-free graphs with nonnegative Bakry–Émery curvature
364405.statement: Let $G$ be a triangle-free graph satisfying $CD(0,\infty)$ with both the unweighted normalized and non-normalized Laplacians. An **induced $k$-cycle conjecture.** $G$ contains no induced $k$-cycle for $k\geq 5$, except for $C_n$ with $n\geq 5$ and several graphs. The conjecture seeks structural restrictions on triangle-free graphs with nonnegative Bakry–Émery curvature; the source notes that many examples consist of $4$-cycles, while a complete classification is not given.

364454.title: Invariant graph conjecture for marked expanding Thurston maps
364454.statement: Let $(F,Q)$ be a marked expanding Thurston map, where $F$ is an expanding Thurston map of the sphere and $Q$ is the marked set. An **$F$-invariant graph** is a graph preserved by $F$. **Invariant graph conjecture.** There exists an $F$-invariant graph containing $Q$. This conjecture, attributed in the source to a problem of Bonk and Meyer, would imply the rational-map conjecture above in the Sierpiński-carpet and sphere Julia-set cases; its general status is not resolved in the supplied text.

364481.title: Injectivity of pairwise products of partition parts
364481.statement:
For a partition $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_\ell)$, let $\operatorname{pre}_2(\lambda)$ be the partition whose parts are the products $\lambda_i\lambda_k$ for $1\leq i<k\leq\ell$. **Pairwise-product injectivity conjecture.** If $\lambda$ and $\mu$ are partitions of $n$ for some $n\geq0$, then

$$
\operatorname{pre}_2(\lambda)=\operatorname{pre}_2(\mu)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\lambda=\mu.
$$

This injectivity would imply the first odd-part dominance inequality above. It is presented as conjectural, with no resolution given in the source.

364512.title: Functoriality of the lasso construction on schemata
364512.statement:
A **schema** is a small category, and for a schema $\mathsf{T}$, $\mathsf{Set}^{\mathsf{T}}$ denotes its associated copresheaf category. Let $\mathsf{Lasso}(\mathsf{Set}^{\mathsf{T}})$ be the category of lassos on that copresheaf category. **Lasso functoriality conjecture.** There is a contravariant functor

$$
\mathsf{Lasso} \colon \mathsf{Cat} \to \mathsf{Cat}
$$

which sends every functor $F \colon \mathsf{S} \to \mathsf{T}$ between schemata to a functor

$$
\mathsf{Lasso}(\mathsf{Set}^{\mathsf{T}}) \to \mathsf{Lasso}(\mathsf{Set}^{\mathsf{S}})
$$

between the corresponding categories of lassos. This would establish a systematic relationship between a schema and the category of lassos on its copresheaf category; the source presents it as a conjecture and does not provide a resolution.

364624.title: Frankl's conjecture for bipartite graphs with exactly one pendant vertex
364624.statement: Let $G$ be a bipartite graph, and call a vertex **pendant** when it has degree one. **Frankl's one-pendant-vertex conjecture.** Every bipartite graph with exactly one pendant vertex satisfies Frankl's conjecture. The source presents this as one of three graph-theoretic conjectures equivalent to the union-closed sets conjecture; its general status is therefore open, although restricted graph classes are proved in the paper.

364715.title: Conjecture on the complexity of the k-general d-position problem
364715.statement: The $k$-general $d$-position problem takes as input a graph $G$, integers $k\geq 2$ and $d\geq 1$, and a positive integer $r$, and asks whether $\mathrm{gp}^k_d(G)$ is greater than $r$. **Complexity conjecture.** The $k$-general $d$-position problem is $\operatorname{NP}$-complete. This conjecture is motivated by the known NP-completeness of the general $d$-position problem. The source does not give a proof or indicate that the conjecture has been resolved.

364748.title: Boundary extremality conjecture for the normalized simplex of spectra
364748.statement:
Let $\mathbb{SL}_1^n$ denote the normalized set of spectra under consideration, let $\partial \mathbb{SL}_1^n$ be its boundary, and let $\mathbb{E}^n$ be its set of extremal points. **Boundary extremality conjecture.** If $n>3$, then

$$
\partial \mathbb{SL}_1^n\subseteq\mathbb{E}^n,
$$

i.e., every point on the boundary is extremal. The conjecture would show that characterizing the extreme points is enough to characterize $\mathbb{SL}_1^n$; it is known to fail when $n=2$ and $n=3$, while its validity for $n>3$ remains open.

364839.title: Characterization of Castelnuovo triplets
364839.statement:
Let $c \geq 2$, $d \geq 3$, and $b \geq d+1$ be integers. A **Castelnuovo triplet** is a triplet $(b,c,d)$ arising from a Castelnuovo lattice polytope with the corresponding parameters.

**Castelnuovo triplet conjecture.** The triplet $(b,c,d)$ is Castelnuovo if and only if

$$
d+1 \leq b \leq cd+(2d+2).
$$

The preceding results establish the sufficiency of the stated bounds in the available range, while the necessity and the full characterization are open for $d \geq 3$. The corresponding assertion is known in dimension $d=2$.

364872.title: The three-sevenths upper-bound conjecture for the isolation game
364872.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $n(G)=|V(G)|$ denote its order, and let $\iota_{\rm g}(G)$ and $\iota_{\rm g}'(G)$ denote the game isolation numbers when Dominator and Staller, respectively, start. A graph has no $K_2$-components if none of its connected components is isomorphic to $K_2$. **Three-sevenths upper-bound conjecture.** For any graph $G$ with no $K_2$-components,

$$
\iota_{\rm g}(G) \leq \left\lceil\frac{3}{7}n(G)\right\rceil \text{ and } \iota_{\rm g}'(G) \leq \left\lceil\frac{3}{7}n(G)\right\rceil.
$$

The conjecture would improve the proved upper bound $\iota_{\rm g}(G)\leq n(G)/2$ for the isolation game. The bound is supported by examples attaining the three-sevenths value, but no proof is given and the conjecture remains open.

364900.title: Klimošová–Piguet–Rohzoň skew-tree conjecture
364900.statement:
Let $r$ be a parameter, let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph, and call a tree $T$ **$r$-skew** if one of its parts has order at most $r|T|$.

**Klimošová–Piguet–Rohzoň conjecture.** If at least $rn$ vertices of $G$ have degree at least $d$, then $G$ contains a copy of every $r$-skew tree with $d$ edges.

This sharpens the Loebl–Komlós–Sós conjecture by incorporating the bipartite skew of the target tree. It is listed among the related unsolved bounded-degree problems.

364925.title: Matching-divisors conjecture for regular quotients and symplectic Pfaffians
364925.statement: Let $X=G/H$ be an affine homogeneous spherical variety with abelian regular centralizers and no type $N$ roots. Let $\mathfrak c=(\mathfrak h^\perp){/\!/}H\simeq\mathfrak c_{G_X^\vee}$, let $\mathfrak D_{ns}\subset\mathfrak c$ be the divisor over which the regular quotient generically has two preimages, and let $\mathfrak D\subset\mathfrak c_{G_X^\vee}$ be the divisor defined by the vanishing of $\mathrm{Pf}_X$. **Matching-divisors conjecture.** Under the natural identification $\mathfrak c\simeq\mathfrak c_{G_X^\vee}$, the divisors $\mathfrak D_{ns}$ and $\mathfrak D$ match exactly. This statement is presented as equivalent to the relative duality conjecture under additional hypotheses, including the regular-centralizer duality conjecture; it is not proved in general.

365072.title: Su and Liu's Ramsey-full equivalence conjecture
365072.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph with no isolated vertex. A graph is **Ramsey-full** if, writing $R(H,H)=N$, there exists a red-blue edge-coloring of $K_N-e$ containing neither a red copy nor a blue copy of $H$. It is **Gallai-Ramsey-full** if, writing $GR_k(H)=N$, there exists a Gallai $k$-edge-coloring of $K_N-e$ using colors from $[k]$ with no monochromatic copy of $H$ in any color.

**Su and Liu's conjecture.** $H$ is Ramsey-full if and only if $H$ is Gallai-Ramsey-full.

Su and Liu observed that complete graphs and cycles of length four have both properties. The conjecture is presented here as open; this paper gives two classes of graphs that are Ramsey-full but not Gallai-Ramsey-full, disproving it.

365080.title: Conlon–Fox–Kwan–Sudakov conjecture on surplus in hypergraph cuts
365080.statement:
Let $r$ and $k$ be integers satisfying

$$
2\leq k\leq r,\qquad r\geq 3,\qquad (r,k)\neq(3,2).
$$

Let $H$ be an $r$-graph with $m$ edges.

**Conlon–Fox–Kwan–Sudakov conjecture.** The surplus should satisfy

$$
\operatorname{sp}_k(H)=\Omega_r(m^{2/3}).
$$

This would establish the conjectured $m^{2/3}$-order improvement for $k$-cuts in $r$-graphs. The paper identifies this as an open problem, excluding the pair $(r,k)=(3,2)$.

365097.title: The additive complexity conjecture for automatic sequences
365097.statement:
Let $k\geq 2$ be an integer, and let $\mathbf{w}$ be a $k$-automatic sequence over a finite set of non-negative integers. Its additive complexity is the function assigning to each positive integer $n$ the number of distinct sums of length-$n$ factors of $\mathbf{w}$.

**Additive complexity conjecture.** The additive complexity of a $k$-automatic sequence is a $k$-regular sequence.

This conjecture extends the analogous conjecture for abelian complexity. The paper proves a particular case, while the general statement remains open.

365116.title: Module-support conjecture for the q=1,2 rows of the LHS spectral sequence
365116.statement: Let $G$ be a 3D space group, and consider the standard Lyndon–Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence for its translation extension. At the $E_2$ page, examine the module structures in the rows with $q=1$ and $q=2$. **Module-support conjecture.** The module generator of each of the $q=1$ and $q=2$ rows can occur only in the columns $p=0$ or $p=1$. This proposed restriction is intended to control the possible degrees of cohomology-ring generators through the spectral-sequence calculation, but remains conjectural.

365134.title: The Hamiltonian-path conjecture for non-conflicting flows
365134.statement: Let $G$ be a bridgeless cubic graph containing a Hamiltonian path, and let $\overline{F}$ denote a $2$-factor of $G$. A **non-conflicting nowhere-zero $Z_2\times Z_2$-flow with respect to $\overline{F}$** is the flow notion defined in the paper. **The Hamiltonian-path flow conjecture.** Unless $G$ is the Petersen graph, there exists a $2$-factor $\overline{F}$ such that $G/\overline{F}$ admits a non-conflicting nowhere-zero $Z_2\times Z_2$-flow with respect to $\overline{F}$. The paper presents this as its final conjecture; it remains open.

365197.title: The linear lower-bound conjecture for small eigenvalues of cusped hyperbolic surfaces
365197.statement:
Let $\mathcal{M}_{g,n}$ denote the moduli space of hyperbolic surfaces of signature $(g,n)$, and call an eigenvalue of the Laplacian **small** when it is less than $\frac{1}{4}$. Here $g$ is the genus and $n$ is the number of cusps.

**Linear small-eigenvalue conjecture.** There are constants $a,b>0$ such that, whenever

$$
n>a\left(g+1\right),
$$

every surface in $\mathcal{M}_{g,n}$ has at least

$$
b\left(2g+n-2\right)
$$

small eigenvalues.

The conjecture would remove the logarithmic loss in the paper's unconditional lower bound and establish an almost linear number of small eigenvalues whenever the number of cusps dominates the genus. The paper presents it as unresolved; its status is therefore open.

365505.title: The wasteful partial linkage hindrance conjecture for finitary matroids
365505.statement:
Let $M$ and $N$ be finitary matroids on a common ground set. For a set $I$, write $M/I$ and $N/I$ for the matroid contractions, and let $r(M/I)$ and $r(N/I)$ denote their ranks. An **$(M,N)$-hindrance** is an $(M,N)$-wave that does not span $N.\mathsf{span}_M(I)$, where an $(M,N)$-wave is a set in $\mathcal{I}(M)\cap\mathcal{I}(N.\mathsf{span}_M(I))$. **Wasteful partial linkage hindrance conjecture.** If there is an $I\in\mathcal{I}(M)\cap\mathcal{I}(N)$ such that

$$
r(M/I)<r(N/I),
$$

then $(M,N)$ is hindered. This proposes a criterion for detecting hindrance in the problem of finding an $M$-independent spanning set of $N$; the supplied text does not indicate whether the conjecture has been resolved.
